narrative.title: Triaging a Packet Queue by Priority Class
narrative.scenario: A router holds packets tagged with one of three priority classes, encoded as 0, 1 and 2. The scheduler must rewrite the queue so class 0 comes first, then class 1, then class 2, with no queue-sized scratch buffer and no library sort. Reorder the queue in place in a single pass.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers where each value is 0, 1 or 2.
narrative.outputFormat: The same array reordered so all 0s come first, followed by all 1s and then all 2s.

testCases.explanation: Both zeros are pulled to the front, both twos to the back, and the ones settle in the middle.
Only three packets, but each class still has to land in its own band.

hintLevels: Level 1: Counting the classes would work, but it needs two passes; consider maintaining three regions that grow towards each other.

Level 2: Keep a low boundary, a middle scanner and a high boundary: swapping into the low side advances both low and the scanner, a class-1 packet just advances the scanner, and a class-2 packet swaps with the high side.
Level 3: When you swap with the high boundary the value you receive has never been inspected, so the scanner must NOT advance there; the walk ends once the scanner passes the high boundary.
